title: Alto saxophone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS alto saxophone (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: Alto saxophone from the measured air column of one Selmer Super Action Series II specimen (McGill CAML's WIAT 0.1.0: 12 bore stations over 1022 mm, 25 holes with their diameters, chimney heights and centres; numbers only, nothing committed), with the fingerings WIAT lists; the earlier stand-in (one straight cone cut to each note's length, no tone holes) is replaced on C4, E3 and F3, and Ab4 and E5, which the stand-in could not play, have pages. The source does not print the serial (438024 is probable), the method or the uncertainty, flags its own bell as needing more precise equipment, differs from Scavone's 1997 data on the same serial by 8 to 40 mm, puts holes 16 and 17 at one station and overlaps holes 2 and 3, and gives no azimuths; the elbow is laid straight (WIAT's comment: about 20 cents) and the key rise h_pad is a typed 2 mm that the card does not use. The reed opening, width and area, the lay profile, the tongue contact row, the reed-noise law, the clarinet's bore-air profile scaled to this bore, the 0.025 m reed channel length with van Zon et al.'s separated-jet law, and the mouthpiece push (solved once on the old stand-in's C4) are the earlier pages' rows, borrowed and not tuned after the read. C4, E3 and F3 are blown at 2785, 2745 and 3040 Pa, the new Ab4 and E5 at C4's 2785 Pa (a stated choice). The open-hole interaction is TMMI's with the monopole mutual impedance replaced by its baffled-piston large-distance form: the monopole load was not passive at 575, 551, 435, 512 and 622 of 941 frequencies on the five fingerings, the piston form is passive at all 941 on all five and its coupling error against the exact pair resistance is at most 4.5e-2 (mean 1.6e-3) on C4's geometry; the receipts list no fallback frequency. Played pitch against equal temperament: C4 +53 c, E3 +8 c, F3 +65 c, Ab4 +55 c; E5's periodicity is an octave below its note (333.07 Hz, E4 + 18 c) with the strongest line at 666.23 Hz (E5 + 18 c). The loose count is 8 of 15 on C4 (the live stand-in page 9), 6 of 14 on E3 (6) and 5 of 14 on F3 (7), 7 of 14 on Ab4 and 5 of 14 on E5. The receiver's grid latency is removed from every clip. The engine's passive impedance from the neck plane agrees with the same specimen's measured maxima at 22 of 27 maxima within 100 cents, as written, below 915 Hz only.
physics_present: The measured air column of WIAT 0.1.0's Selmer Super Action Series II alto (12 bore stations over 1022 mm to a 119 mm bell, 25 holes: 23 tone holes, the neck vent of 1.70 mm and the body vent of 2.15 mm, with WIAT's diameters, minimum chimney heights and centres), the fingerings "A 1", "D flat 1", "D 1", "F 2" and "D flat 3" for C4, E3, F3, Ab4 and E5 (written pitch is the concert note plus a major sixth); the curved elbow laid straight over its centreline length

An alto reed fitted to a Lefebvre mouthpiece (mass per area 0.0475 kg/m2, resonance 1500 Hz and damping 0.6 of the angular resonance, from Table A.1 of Lefebvre 2010, a Meyer #8 mouthpiece on a cone); its opening 1.7 mm, width 10 mm and area 7.5e-5 m2 are borrowed, the area being printed only as the illustrative common parameter of Lefebvre's Figs. A.3 and A.4, whose reeds have 0.075 kg/m2 and 1000 Hz; the card's mass 3.5625e-6 kg is 0.0475 kg/m2 times that area
One mouthpiece position for every note, pushed in 13.2693 mm, solved once on the old stand-in's C4 passive peak against equal temperament and not solved again on this air column
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two alto players
Reed noise, the duct-constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990), extrapolated, with no level set against a recording

A flanged bell radiating into room air with ISO 9613 absorption, 0.5 m on axis, a receiver of 96 rings by 256 points, at 48 kHz; the flanged radiation load of the 59.5 mm bell is admitted to ka 28 (checked on the full 16-mode matrix at 7.6e-14)
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)

Bore air along the duct: Noreland 2013's measured temperature profile of a clarinet bore (304.15 K to 294.96 K, borrowed), exhaled breath with saturated water vapour, as a continuous gas field; the positions are scaled to the saxophone's bore by this model's choice (1.0783 m / 0.6552 m); the body slope, the cuts and the push are re-solved on it

A reed lay profile in place of the default slit lay (stiffness 6.1725e6, exponent 2.0, onset 0.16 mm, Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0): the stiffness is Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012's printed contact stiffness per area for a clarinet reed times this reed's face area, the other three are the clarinet cards' values; borrowed, no saxophone lay is printed

A tongue contact row on the reed from the blow's start (area 2.6e-5 m2, force 0.2 N, effective area 7.5e-5 m2, released from 0.1845 s over 5 ms): the area an assumption of this model (the 2 mm bare length of the tongue-sensor wire of Li 2016a times the 13 mm width of a clarinet reed; no tongue contact area is printed in Li 2016a or 2016b) and a clarinet's force (Almeida 2017), with the release start set by Hofmann 2012's printed 34.5 ms alto tonguing contact time

The reed channel's flow law: the separated-jet law of van Zon et al. 1990 (measured on a two-dimensional clarinet mouthpiece; its eq. 7 is inconsistent with its eq. 5, so the Poiseuille part is a construction from its eqs. 1, 5 and 6) at the cards' `slit_length 0.025` m, the clarinet cards' lay length, borrowed; quasisteady, laminar

The receiver's grid latency (a quarter of its grid: 2048 samples, 42.7 ms, on C4; 4096 samples, 85.3 ms, on E3 and F3) was removed from the start of every clip on 2026-11-08 with `--compensate-outlet-latency`: each new clip is the previous version's render shifted by those samples, equal to the last bit, so there is no new physics, only the timing; on E3 and F3 the release tail the old clip cut off is now heard (rms 12.5 and 10.0 LSB over the last 4096 samples). The loose count moves from 10 to 9 of 15 on C4 (C4 fall), and stays 6 of 14 on E3 and 7 of 14 on F3 (strict 5 to 4 on E3), because the grader cuts from the detected onset to the end of the clip and removing the latency moves that onset earlier by the same time, so the cut is that much longer; the partial-trajectory measure is the one that crosses its ruler on C4 and E3.

Hole lengths, `tonehole_lengths lefebvre-scavone-2012` (Lefebvre and Scavone, JASA 131, 2012): all 25 holes lie inside the printed diameter-to-bore range (b/a 0.088 to 0.738); the vents' chimney ratios (t/b 5.9 and 1.9) have no stated range, and the set is printed for ka up to 1, which these mouths pass at about 2.7 kHz

Open-hole interaction, `open_hole_interaction tmmi 2 piston`: TMMI's mutual impedance with the point monopole replaced by its baffled-piston large-distance form (monopole times the directivities 2 J1(ka)/(ka) of both mouths, factor 2 kept); not the exact pair integral, with the measured coupling error against the exact pair resistance on C4's geometry of 1.6e-3 mean and 4.5e-2 maximum; passive at all 941 frequencies (500 to 24000 Hz) on all five fingerings with the engine's own self load, where the monopole form fails at 575, 551, 435, 512 and 622; no frequency falls back to independent holes

Check against the same specimen's measured impedance, never a selector: the engine's passive input impedance from the neck-input plane (no mouthpiece rows, unflanged termination as the measured instrument radiates, so only the first one to three maxima below 915 Hz, where the unflanged load of this bell reaches ka 1) for the ten fingering files of serial 438024 (A, B, B flat, C, medium C, medium C sharp, D, E, F, G), WIAT as written. Of 27 engine maxima, 9 lie within 30 cents of a measured maximum within 20 dB of the strongest, 22 within 100 cents and 25 within 200 cents; 2 have none within 200 cents; every file has at least one within 100 cents, and six files (B flat, C, D, E, F, G) one within 30. The check was run with the monopole mutual impedance and before the piston form; it was not repeated. The reading with holes 21 to 24 moved by +21.5 mm was swept as well and is not used: provenance decides, as written.
physics_missing: Pads, key rise, hole azimuths and a measured specimen identity: WIAT's h_pad is a typed 2 mm and is not used; no azimuth is given; the serial is not printed and the method and uncertainty are not stated; the bell is flagged by its own file; holes 16 and 17 share a station and holes 2 and 3 overlap; the elbow is laid straight (about 20 cents by WIAT's own comment)
A measured alto reed opening, width and area: the opening is an unplayed-tip upper bound, the width a tenor reed's and the area Lefebvre's illustrative value

The right pitch: the three sit +30.8, -6.1 and -3.6 c from equal temperament, a 37 c spread, with the passive peaks (solved without the lay and tongue rows) within 0.3 c of it; the spread is the reed's pull, which differs by note, and why is not shown
The recordings' spectra and noise: harmonics-to-noise reads 1.1 to 3.6 dB above the recordings on all three notes, and C4's centroid is 1203 Hz against 403 Hz

The second register's note: Ab4 and E5 now sound, with the neck vent and the body vent of the measured specimen. Ab4 plays +55 c from equal temperament; E5's periodicity is 333.07 Hz, an octave below its note, with the strongest line at 666.23 Hz (E5 + 18 c); why the reed locks to the lower period is not shown. The reed, lay and tongue rows are the clarinet cards' and the pressure is C4's

A same-specimen impedance for comparison above 915 Hz or with the piston form: the check covers each file's first one to three maxima below 915 Hz (the unflanged load of this bell reaches ka 1 there), 22 of 27 engine maxima within 100 cents of a measured one, run with the monopole form and not repeated; the measured files do not give the specimen's radiation, so a flanged comparison is not possible

A measured saxophone bore-air profile: the field is a clarinet's, its position scaling to the saxophone's bore is this model's choice, and E3's lock falls from 1.000 to 0.978 on this air without a traced cause

A saxophone reed's lay and tongue: no lay profile or tongue force is printed for a saxophone and no tongue contact area is printed for any reed (the 2 mm of Li 2016a is the bare length of its tongue-sensor wire, not a contact length), so the rows are a clarinet's with one alto number (Hofmann 2012's 34.5 ms contact time); the count does not move with them on any of the three notes, and the render's reed-opening trace was not read to show what the tongue row does

The reed channel's length and law: no saxophone channel length is printed, and 0.025 m is the clarinet cards' lay length. The clarinet mouthpiece's printed channel length, 1.4 mm, puts this reed (openings 0.46 to 1.9 mm) at L/h about 1 to 3, on the law's contracted branch, and the law's step at L/h = 3 (a jump with no blend in the print) stopped the render on C4 and F3 (the massive reed's implicit contact solve did not resolve the momentum balance) and cost E3 four measures. The print's data below L/h = 3 give a constant 0.45 +- 0.05 without a stated range of L/h. Unsteady channel inertia is not modelled.

The right pitch: the five sit +53, +8, +65, +55 c from equal temperament on C4, E3, F3 and Ab4 and an octave low by periodicity on E5; no mouthpiece position, bore value or pressure was changed after the read, so the offsets are the measured specimen's geometry with this reed's pull
